finding.approach: H-A-refined — distance-gated, feature-anchored derivation (the steelman of the PRIMARY hypothesis): derive topic->vehicle edges from the 80k enrichments, but replace naive max-overlap with selective-match-at-distance: (1) embedding cosine-distance band between synset_centroids (cross-domain gate), (2) >=1 shared HIGH-salience curated cluster whose dominant_type DIFFERS from the topic's dominant property-type (selective cross-type feature match), (3) a Lakoff concreteness gradient (vehicle more concrete than topic). Objective = selective-match-at-distance, not max-overlap.
finding.method: Each leg produces a context-free signal from existing tables (zero per-topic LLM): synset_centroids (300d FastText) -> cross-domain distance; synset_properties_curated JOIN vocab_clusters.dominant_type -> typed feature overlap (the dominant_type column is already populated: 7,681/7,728 curated clusters carry a non-null/non-other type, consistent within each cluster); synset_concreteness -> gradient. Candidate edges = pairs passing the distance band AND carrying a cross-type shared cluster AND a positive concreteness gradient; rank/threshold by a combined score. As a PROPOSER (not scorer) it would feed surviving candidates to a cheap LLM verifier; the question this approach must answer is whether the gate is selective enough to make that verification cheap.
finding.measured_result: Computed on the real 2000+2000-style spike cohort (1067 apt + 582 inapt pairs that snap to synsets). Harness: docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/ha_refined_separability.py (committed, reproducible). ROC-AUC (apt vs inapt) per leg, with 1000-sample bootstrap CI: concr_grad_lemma (sense-agnostic concreteness gradient) = 0.745 [0.720,0.769]; concr_grad_snap = 0.730 [0.703,0.757]; cos_dist alone = 0.579 [0.545,0.613]; neg_shared_curated (fewer shared = better, the M02 family) = 0.581 [0.554,0.605]; CROSS_TYPE_SHARED (the assigned centrepiece) = 0.439 [0.419,0.462] — BELOW RANDOM, CI entirely under 0.5; dist+0.15*grad = 0.736 (does NOT beat gradient alone, 0.745). Per inapt class the gradient is strong exactly where the quality bar bites: same_domain 0.814, synonym_or_hypernym 0.803, wrong_concreteness 0.766; weak on dead_metaphor 0.612. Structural fact: 70% of APT pairs share ZERO curated cluster vs 57% of inapt -> REQUIRING a shared feature discards most live metaphors. Command: python3 docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/ha_refined_separability.py --db data-pipeline/output/lexicon_v2.db --apt data-pipeline/output/metaphor_spike_apt_phase2_20260525T004154.jsonl --inapt data-pipeline/output/metaphor_spike_inapt_phase2_20260525T004154.jsonl --bootstrap 1000 -o ha_refined_result.json
finding.variance: Bootstrap 95% CIs reported above (1000 resamples, n=1067 apt / 582 inapt). Headline gradient AUC CI [0.720,0.769] is tight and clears 0.5 decisively. The cross_type_shared CI [0.419,0.462] is entirely below 0.5 — its failure is not noise. Residual uncontrolled variance: (a) sense-snapping noise (80% of cohort words are multi-sense, F4/C13) — controlled by computing the gradient sense-agnostically (lemma-mean), which actually RAISED AUC 0.730->0.745, evidence the signal is not a snap artefact; (b) the cohort is a single Sonnet-generated apt/inapt set with base rate 0.645, not Julian-graded — see quality_risks. AUC bounded; the production-precision number is NOT bounded by this cohort.
finding.quality_outcome: Against the LIVE/cross-domain bar: the assigned feature-anchoring mechanism FAILS to surface live-over-dead. cross_type_shared is anti-correlated (0.439) and the full curated-overlap family sits at ~0.58 — this directly extends M02's null from scoring to candidate-gen, confirming F1. The 70%-zero-overlap fact means feature-anchoring would throw away the majority of genuine cross-domain metaphors (idea->light, anger->fire both have 0 shared curated clusters). What survives is ONE real quality signal: the Lakoff concreteness gradient (AUC 0.745), which IS aligned with the bar — it most cleanly separates apt from the same_domain / synonym_or_hypernym / wrong_concreteness inapt classes (the dead/synonym cases the product must reject). But it is weak on dead_metaphor (0.612), and as a single weak feature it cannot certify an edge as live on its own — it can only concentrate apt pairs ahead of a verifier.
finding.cost_at_100k: This approach generates ZERO edges by itself with zero API spend (the derivation + gradient gate are pure SQL over existing tables; harness runs in ~seconds for the cohort, scales to a few minutes for 100k via the existing inverted-index in derive_candidates.py). All cost is in the verification tier it feeds. Using the $0.07 cold-call / cache-amortised model: the gradient gate at thr>=1.0 keeps 57% of apt while cutting inapt volume ~2.6x (precision 0.645->0.824 on cohort), so it reduces the verification call budget proportionally. If verification is a batched Haiku judge (~$0.07 amortised toward per-token floor in 5-min cache windows, ~$0.003-0.01/call in-batch) over, say, 10 surviving candidates/topic: ~100k topics x 10 = ~1M judge calls. The gradient pre-filter removes the inapt-heavy tail BEFORE that call, so it does not add cost — it SAVES roughly the inapt fraction it screens. Net standalone spend of THIS approach: ~$0 (no generation). Assumption: gate runs offline once; verification cost is owned by H-B/H-D, not by H-A-refined.
finding.scale_math: Arithmetic from cohort to 100k: the gate's discriminative value is AUC 0.745 [0.720,0.769] (measured, n=1649 pairs). REFUSAL TO EXTRAPOLATE A PRODUCTION PRECISION: the cohort base rate is 0.645 (65% apt by construction); the wild base rate when deriving candidates over the 100k x (df-capped ~hundreds of candidates) substrate is far lower (live cross-domain pairs are rare among all distance-banded pairs), so cohort precision (0.824 at thr=1.0) does NOT transfer to production precision. A gate of AUC ~0.75 applied to a low-prior candidate pool yields a modest precision lift, not a high-precision edge set. Concretely: if the true wild prior of 'live' among distance+gradient-passing pairs is p, post-gate precision ~ p*TPR / (p*TPR + (1-p)*FPR) with TPR/FPR from the ROC at the chosen operating point (thr=1.0: TPR 0.567, FPR 0.220). At p=0.10 that is ~0.22; at p=0.05 ~0.12. So the gate alone CANNOT meet a high-precision bar at 100k; it is a volume-reducing PRE-FILTER, not an edge producer. Confidence: high on the AUC and its CI; high on the refutation of feature-anchoring; the production-precision figure is deliberately unbounded by this cohort.
finding.quality_risks: (1) The centrepiece (cross-type selective feature match) is measured anti-correlated (AUC 0.439) — building on it would actively select dead/same-domain pairs. (2) Requiring ANY shared curated feature discards 70% of live metaphors (the live cohort's signal is NOT in shared curated features). (3) The surviving gradient signal is a proxy for Lakoff abstract->concrete directionality; it will MIS-fire on concrete-topic metaphors and on dead_metaphor (AUC 0.612), and could bias the graph toward only abstract->concrete edges, starving concrete topics. (4) Cohort is Sonnet-generated apt/inapt, not Julian-graded (n=11 human labels, G4) — the AUC is against a model's notion of aptness, so it inherits that model's biases; must be re-checked against the 11 + a fresh LLM-judge calibrated to them before trusting the operating point. (5) Sense-snapping noise (80% multi-sense) — mitigated for the gradient via lemma-mean but unmitigated for the distance/feature legs.
finding.harness_design: Committed and RUN: docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/ha_refined_separability.py (pure SQL+Python, no API). It (a) snaps each spike (topic,vehicle) surface pair to synsets, (b) computes per-leg features {cos_dist over synset_centroids; n_shared and cross_type_shared over synset_properties_curated JOIN vocab_clusters.dominant_type; concr gradient both sense-snapped and lemma-mean}, (c) reports ROC-AUC + bootstrap CI per leg, operating points (precision/recall vs gradient threshold), and per-inapt-reason-type AUC. Result JSON: artifacts/ha_refined_result.json. To extend to a production candidate-gen dry-run the orchestrator can: reuse artifacts/derive_candidates.py to enumerate df-capped candidates for a <=20-topic cohort, then apply the gradient+distance gate from this harness as a post-filter and hand the survivors to the LLM judge — measuring how much inapt volume the gate removes before any API spend.
finding.depends_on_separability: This approach IS the separability experiment for the feature-anchored family, and I have already run it. If the orchestrator's apt-vs-inapt separability experiment SUCCEEDS for some OTHER function (e.g. a learned combination), it will most likely be carried by the concreteness gradient (the one leg here that separates, AUC 0.745) — H-A-refined's contribution then narrows to 'use the free gradient + distance band as a pre-filter to cut verification volume', and verdict moves toward viable-as-prefilter (never viable-as-standalone-edge-producer). If the separability experiment FAILS (no context-free function separates apt from inapt above ~0.6 net of base rate), then this approach is NOT_VIABLE in any form and the mission must fall back to per-topic generation + judging (H-B/H-C/H-D), with H-A contributing only recall candidates, never admitted edges.
finding.one_line: The assigned feature-anchoring centrepiece (cross-type selective match) is measured anti-correlated (AUC 0.439, CI<0.5) and the whole curated-overlap family confirms M02's null — but the steelman salvages one real free signal, the Lakoff concreteness gradient (AUC 0.745 [0.72,0.77]), which works only as a verification-volume pre-filter, never as a standalone high-precision edge producer.

finding.approach: H-B — embedding ANN band (top-b nearest synsets per topic over the 81,185 FastText synset_centroids) as candidate generation, then a cheap single Haiku call per (topic,vehicle) judging live/dead/irrelevant to supply precision. Not generation.
finding.method: For each topic synset, rank all 81,185 synset_centroids by cosine; the top-b form the candidate band (recall layer). Each candidate is then verified by one batched Haiku live/dead/irrelevant call (precision layer). Edges admitted = band candidates the verifier labels live. Pick b at the precision/recall/cost knee; the verifier converts band recall into edge precision. Per F6, the band has recall but poor precision; H-B's bet is that the verify step is cheap enough and the band's apt-recall high enough that the product is favourable.
finding.measured_result: MEASURED, reproducible (cmd: `python3 docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hb_band_recall.py`). On the spike cohort (185 snappable topics, 986 gold apt pairs, 535 gold inapt pairs; union/best-case snap over all topic senses): APT BAND RECALL = recall@10 0.5%, @50 4.6%, @200 12.9%, @1000 30.8%, @5000 62.8%; median apt vehicle sits at RANK 2,870 of 81,185 (p25 685, p75 8,642, p90 19,724, max 74,088). To recall 50% of apt vehicles needs b~=2,870/topic; 90% needs b~=20,000/topic. ANTI-SIGNAL (the killer): at EVERY band the INAPT vehicles are recalled at a HIGHER rate than apt — apt:inapt odds ratio 0.08 (b=10), 0.26 (b=50), 0.41 (b=200), 0.56 (b=1000); always <1.0. Canaries: anger->fire rank 19, anger->kettle 9,520, time->river 13,141, hope->horizon 15,162 — the live literary metaphors are buried deepest. Realistic single-sense ('first') snap is the same or worse. NEEDS_ORCHESTRATOR_RUN for the Haiku verify precision-on-band number (any live `claude` call; I ran no API).
finding.variance: Cluster-robust (topic-clustered) 2,000-sample bootstrap over the 185 topics: apt recall@200 12.9% 95% CI [10.6%, 15.1%]; @1000 30.8% [27.1%, 34.5%]; @2870 50.0% [46.0%, 53.9%]. CIs are tight — this is not a small-sample artifact. The apt:inapt odds-ratio<1 holds across all bands and both snap policies, so the anti-correlation is robust to snapping noise. Residual uncertainty: the spike cohort's apt/inapt sets are Sonnet/Haiku-authored, not Julian-graded (only n=11 human labels exist, G4); if those gold labels are biased the absolute recall could shift, but the structural finding (cross-domain apt vehicles rank below same-domain inapt ones) follows from FastText measuring distributional similarity and would not reverse.
finding.quality_outcome: FAILS the LIVE/cross-domain bar at the mechanism level, not just the cost level. FastText cosine measures distributional co-occurrence similarity; live cross-domain metaphor is by construction a leap to a DIFFERENT domain, so apt vehicles are FAR in embedding space while the near band is dominated by synonyms, co-hyponyms and same-domain near-misses — exactly the inapt set (anger->passion, anger->poison rank above anger->fire/kettle). This is the same surface F1 found for feature-overlap (maximise similarity => dead metaphor) re-confirmed in embedding space, and it matches F6/G8. The band actively de-prioritises the product target. A downstream Haiku verifier can only raise precision, never recall: if the apt edge is not in the band it can never be admitted, so the 12.9%@200 / 50%@2870 recall ceiling caps the whole approach regardless of verifier quality.
finding.cost_at_100k: Verify-only cost (band gen is free local numpy/faiss), J=25 candidates/Haiku call, $0.0725 CLI cold floor (G6) + tokens. Pessimistic = every call cold; optimistic = 95% cache_read. To reach the cheapest *useful* recall the band must be large because the band is inapt-enriched: b=200 (13% recall) = 800k calls = $6k–$61k; b=2,870 (50% recall) = 11.5M calls = $86k–$878k; b=20,000 (90% recall) = 80M calls = $600k–$6.1M. Generation baseline (2 calls/topic, 200k calls) = $0.7k–$14.5k. So H-B costs 6x–60x the baseline to recover HALF the apt edges, and an even worse fraction of that spend is wasted verifying the inapt-enriched majority of each band. Fails the <=4x spend rule by 1–2 orders of magnitude.
finding.scale_math: Cohort: 185 topics, 986 apt pairs. Recall is pair-level, topic-clustered-bootstrapped (tight CIs above), so it generalises to the population the spike cohort represents (concrete + abstract Forge topics). Extrapolation to 100k topics: assume similar apt-vehicle rank distribution (the mechanism — cross-domain => far in FastText — is topic-agnostic, and abstract topics are WORSE per F3/canaries time/hope). Band b needed for recall R is read off the measured rank curve (R=50% => b~=2,870). Calls = 100,000 * b / J. With J=25: 50%-recall costs 11.5M Haiku calls. I REFUSE to extrapolate a *precision* number for the verifier (no API run; would be fabrication) — but precision cannot rescue recall, and recall is already measured-fatal, so the verdict does not depend on the unmeasured verifier precision.
finding.quality_risks: (1) Inapt-enrichment: the band's nearest neighbours are systematically same-domain near-synonyms and the labelled inapt vehicles, so the verifier faces a hostile base rate and any verifier false-positive admits a dead/synonym edge — the exact failure mode F1 flagged. (2) Recall ceiling: live literary metaphors (time->river, anger->kettle, hope->horizon) are the deepest-ranked, i.e. the product's best edges are the ones H-B is structurally worst at finding. (3) Polysemy/snapping (F4/C13): a vehicle counts via ANY of its median-4 senses (I used the generous union); the realistic noisy single-sense snap is no better and often worse. (4) FastText centroids are property-averaged (synset_centroids = mean of property-word vectors), inheriting the same dead-metaphor bias as the property substrate, not an independent signal.
finding.harness_design: Committed and run: `docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hb_band_recall.py` (pure numpy+sqlite, API-free). It loads synset_centroids into an 81,185x300 matrix, L2-normalises, snaps each spike topic (first|union sense policy) and gold apt/inapt vehicle lemmas via the `lemmas` table, ranks all synsets by cosine, and reports apt/inapt hit-counts per band plus per-topic apt min-ranks to /tmp/hb_band_recall_per_topic.json. Analysis one-liners (also runnable): percentiles + recall thresholds over the per-topic JSON, and topic-clustered bootstrap CIs (seed=7, 2000 resamples). The ONLY missing piece needing API spend is verifier precision-on-band: orchestrator harness = sample ~200 (topic,vehicle) pairs from the b=200 band per a ~20-topic cohort, one batched Haiku live/dead/irrelevant call per J=25, parse total_cost_usd, score against the gold apt/inapt labels and the n=11 human labels; report apt-precision-on-band and admitted-edge apt-rate vs the generation baseline. But run only if a stakeholder wants to confirm the (already-fatal) recall result — recall caps it regardless.
finding.depends_on_separability: My result largely PRE-EMPTS that experiment for the embedding axis: the apt-vs-inapt context-free separability of FastText cosine is exactly what I measured, and it is NEGATIVE (inapt ranks ABOVE apt; odds<1 at all bands). If the orchestrator's separability experiment SUCCEEDS using some OTHER context-free function (e.g. concreteness-gap or property-type-diversity, not raw embedding cosine), then a re-ranked band could lift apt recall and H-B might become a viable RECALL layer under that re-ranker — re-run my harness ranking by the winning function instead of cosine to re-measure. If it FAILS (no context-free function separates apt from inapt), H-B is conclusively dead: no cheap proposer exists and per-topic LLM generation is unavoidable. Either way, plain-cosine ANN is not the proposer.
finding.one_line: Embedding ANN bands are anti-correlated with aptness — inapt vehicles outrank apt ones at every band size and the median apt vehicle is buried at rank 2,870/81k — so the band cannot be a high-precision (or even high-recall) proposer, and verifying a band large enough to recall half the apt edges costs 6x–60x the generation baseline: not_viable.

finding.approach: H-C — distill the 2000-apt/2000-inapt spike cohort into a cheap context-free classifier (logistic regression over embedding cos-dist, concreteness gap/gradient, shared-curated-cluster count, idf-weighted overlap, M05 type-diversity, polysemy, property-count) so it becomes a near-free edge proposer/pre-filter and the LLM drops to spot-checking.
finding.method: Resolve each (topic, vehicle) pair to synsets via lookup_primary_synset, compute 11 context-free features purely from lexicon_v2.db (synset_centroids, synset_concreteness, synset_properties_curated x vocab_clusters, property_vocab_curated.polysemy), label apt=1/inapt=0, train StandardScaler+LogisticRegression under topic-grouped 5-fold CV (GroupKFold prevents topic leakage), read out-of-fold scores as the proposer ranking. Edges = pairs above an operating-point threshold; survivors go to an LLM verifier. Viability thresholds: AUC >=0.85 for a standalone live-edge proposer; >=0.75 usable only as a recall-preserving pre-filter, not standalone.
finding.measured_result: MEASURED (I ran it, zero API). Command: data-pipeline/.venv/bin/python3 docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hc_fast_multivariate.py (writes artifacts/hc_multivariate_result.json). On 984 apt + 525 inapt resolved pairs over 200 topics: topic-grouped 5-fold logistic-regression ROC-AUC = 0.764 +/- 0.022 (folds 0.766/0.775/0.727/0.760/0.795). Single-feature AUCs: concr_grad_lemma 0.746, concr_gap_snap 0.734, pcount_v 0.584, cos_dist 0.574; all shared-feature/type/polysemy features 0.50-0.53 (chance). Coefficients: concr_grad_lemma 0.704 dominates; the full 11-feature model beats the single concreteness feature by only +0.018 AUC — effectively a one-feature (abstract-topic -> concrete-vehicle) classifier. Per-inapt-class AUC: synonym_or_hypernym 0.878, same_domain 0.838, wrong_concreteness 0.777, single_dimension 0.743, dead_metaphor 0.608. Independently corroborated by the pre-existing artifacts/ha_refined_result.json (concr_grad_lemma AUC 0.745, bootstrap CI 0.717-0.770).
finding.variance: Reported CI is cross-fold std: AUC 0.764 +/- 0.022 (5 topic-grouped folds; min 0.727, max 0.795). ha_refined bootstrap (1000x) on the dominant single feature gives CI 0.717-0.770. These bound sampling noise on THIS cohort only. Two variances that CANNOT be bounded from this data: (1) label-source variance — apt/inapt labels are LLM-self-generated, not human, so there is an unmeasured systematic gap to Julian's live/dead judgement (human ground truth n=11 never enters train/test); (2) base-rate variance — the cohort is an artificial ~2:1 apt:inapt enrichment, so any PRECISION figure has unbounded variance when transported to the true (much lower) apt prior over random 100k candidate pairs. AUC is base-rate-invariant and transfers; precision does not.
finding.quality_outcome: FAILS the LIVE/literary bar as a standalone proposer. The classifier separates apt from STRUCTURAL near-misses (synonym/same-domain/concreteness-mismatch, AUC 0.78-0.88) but is near-blind to the product's #1 exclusion target: apt-vs-dead_metaphor AUC = 0.608. Measured dead-metaphor leakage: at 70% apt recall 54% of dead metaphors survive; at 80% recall 64% survive; even at 50% recall 38% survive. Mechanism: dead/conventional metaphors ARE abstract->concrete mappings (that is how they conventionalised), so the one feature carrying the signal (concreteness gradient: apt mean +1.20 vs dead +0.76 — both strongly positive) cannot tell a live cross-domain leap from a dead cliche. Shared-feature overlap features sit at chance (0.50-0.53), re-confirming M02's null and extending it: the only context-free signal is concreteness, which cannot police the live/dead boundary the product depends on.
finding.cost_at_100k: Classifier inference is ~free (no LLM): one-off seconds-long fit on already-paid-for data; scoring 100k topics x K candidate vehicles is pure CPU. Cost is entirely the residual LLM verify rate the AUC forces. Using the $0.07 cold-call / cache-amortised model (~2 calls/topic baseline ~ 200k calls at 100k topics, batched to amortise the 57k-token cache floor): because AUC 0.764 only RANKS and cannot certify live-vs-dead, every admitted edge still needs LLM verification to keep dead metaphors out — the spot-check rate is NOT reducible below ~100% of admitted edges for the live/dead decision. H-C therefore does not cut the per-edge LLM count for the binding judgement; it can only prune the CANDIDATE fan-out fed to the LLM (drop wrong-direction pairs before verify). Net: ~same ~$0.07-amortised per verified edge as baseline; the only saving is fewer wasted verify calls on structural junk, ~1.5-2x candidate-fan-out reduction at keep-top-50%, NOT a reduction to 'spot-checking'. The 'near-free proposer' framing is not achieved.
finding.scale_math: Cohort to 100k. AUC 0.764 +/- 0.022 is base-rate-invariant and transfers as a ranking quality. Precision does NOT: cohort apt base rate 0.652 is an artificial ~2:1 enrichment; over random 100k topic-vehicle candidate pairs the apt prior is far lower (single-digit % at best), so measured precision@k (91% at keep-top-10%, 82% at keep-top-50%) are strict UPPER BOUNDS and I refuse to extrapolate them to a production precision — that honestly needs a fresh cohort sampled at the true candidate prior, which does not exist. What transfers: as a pre-filter at keep-top-50% you discard ~50% of candidate verify calls while retaining ~63% of apt edges (measured apt_recall 0.63) — a ~2x candidate-fan-out reduction, NOT a 4x cost collapse, and it preserves the dead-metaphor problem downstream. Confidence: AUC transfer MEDIUM-HIGH (clean topic-grouped CV, tight CI, corroborated by an independent script); precision transfer NONE (explicit refusal — base-rate shift + LLM-label provenance unquantified).
finding.quality_risks: (1) Label provenance — apt/inapt are LLM-self-generated; the inapt set is the SAME model's taxonomy of structural failures, so the classifier learns to agree with that model, not Julian. The 11 human labels are too few to validate this and never enter the experiment (Invariant #2). (2) Dead-metaphor blindness (AUC 0.608) is product-fatal — the filter passes exactly what the product must reject. (3) One-feature fragility — 0.704/0.018 of the lift is concreteness gradient; the rest is decoration. Concreteness gradient INVERTS on the Lakoff cohort (G8: anger->umbrella is HIGH-concreteness inapt), so the single load-bearing feature is cohort-polarity-dependent and will hurt the cohort it was not tuned on. (4) Sense-snapping noise (F4/C13: anger->'make angry', heart->'playing card') corrupts centroid and concreteness inputs; lemma-mean mitigates, does not remove. (5) Calibration is good (pred 0.85 -> empirical 0.89) but calibrated to the WRONG target (LLM labels), giving false confidence about live-ness.
finding.harness_design: Two API-free scripts, both runnable by the orchestrator. PRIMARY (I ran this): docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hc_fast_multivariate.py — bulk-loads synset_centroids, joins synset_concreteness/synset_properties_curated/vocab_clusters/property_vocab_curated, resolves the apt+inapt spike jsonls via lookup_primary_synset, builds 11 context-free features, runs GroupKFold(5) StandardScaler+LogisticRegression(class_weight=balanced), emits grouped-CV AUC mean/std/folds, single-feature AUCs, mean|coef|, precision@topk (10/25/50/75/100%), a 10-bin calibration curve (pred_mean vs empirical_apt), dead_metaphor leakage at fixed apt-recall (50-90%), per-inapt-class OOF AUC. Run: data-pipeline/.venv/bin/python3 docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hc_fast_multivariate.py (writes hc_multivariate_result.json; ~3-4 min, dominated by the 81k-centroid load). REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP to make the verdict robust to label provenance, both <=20-synset cohorts within G7: (a) re-run the SAME harness but replace LLM inapt labels with a held-out gold cohort of <=20 fresh pairs graded live/dead/irrelevant by Julian (or an Opus judge calibrated to the 11 human labels), report classifier AUC against THOSE labels — if it collapses toward 0.5 on human live/dead (as the 0.608 dead sub-AUC predicts), H-C is conclusively dead; (b) add a 'random-uniform vehicle' negative arm to estimate true candidate-prior precision and remove the artificial 2:1 base rate.
finding.depends_on_separability: My harness IS the separability experiment run on the H-C feature set. If the orchestrator's parallel apt-vs-inapt run SUCCEEDS (high AUC) it will agree with mine (~0.76) — but that number measures separability against LLM-generated structural near-misses, NOT live/dead — so 'separability succeeds' does NOT rescue H-C: the per-class breakdown shows the success is concentrated on structural junk (0.84-0.88) and absent on dead metaphor (0.61). If the separability run FAILS (~0.5), H-C is dead outright. Either way H-C's fate hinges on the SECONDARY question my follow-up isolates — does the signal survive when the negative class is DEAD/CLICHE (the product target) rather than structural near-miss? Measured answer here = no (0.608). So my verdict is robust to the headline separability outcome and turns on the dead-vs-live sub-separability, which already measures as non-viable.
finding.one_line: A context-free classifier distilled from the spike cohort ranks apt-vs-inapt at AUC 0.764 but the signal is essentially one feature (concreteness gradient) that is near-blind to dead metaphors (AUC 0.608, ~54% dead leakage at 70% apt recall) — so it can prune structural junk as a pre-filter but cannot be the near-free LIVE-metaphor proposer the product needs; not viable as designed.

finding.approach: H-D — tiered model routing economics (where FURTHER routing beyond the existing Haiku-propose -> Sonnet-refine baseline cuts 100k cost without quality loss)
finding.method: The graph's metaphor_link arm is the only arm needing per-topic LLM generation. The baseline already routes: Haiku proposes 10 vehicles + flat feature sets, Sonnet refines them into 10 ordered context-free-hop chains (~2 calls/topic). Three further-routing options were costed: (b) Haiku-only — collapse to 1 call/topic by baking Sonnet-written gold few-shots into Haiku's template at load time (the measured "Sonnet-as-prompt-engineer" pattern), so no Sonnet runs at request time; (c) banded — Haiku for all topics, escalate to Sonnet ONLY on a context-free uncertainty band (Haiku self-reported confidence < tau OR topic-vehicle FastText cosine >= tau_same_domain, i.e. same-domain => dead-metaphor risk, the exact failure Sonnet uniquely catches); (d) Opus only as a one-time calibration/spot-check, never per-topic. The cost mechanism is dominated not by which model proposes but by the CLI's 57k-token system-prompt cache: cold calls pay a cache-WRITE floor, warm calls (same prefix within the 5-min window, i.e. sustained batching) pay only cache-READ, amortising the overhead to near-zero.
finding.measured_result: DECOMPOSED the $0.0725 cold Haiku probe (G6): 57,279 cache-creation tok x $1.25/MTok = $0.0716 = 98.7% of the call. The "$0.07 cold floor" IS the CLI system prompt, not the metaphor content (content ~$0.001). [repro: python3 inline, shown below in harness]. VALIDATED against three REAL Metaforge runs (PIPELINE.md L173 / spike-findings L42): Phase1a 20 calls/$0.28=$0.0140/call; Phase1b 40 calls/$0.41=$0.0102/call; Phase2 200 topics/400 Haiku calls/~$2=$0.0050/call. The Phase2 $0.005/call decomposes as $0.0042 pure content + ~$0.0008 amortised cache (=~4 cold-writes spread over 400 calls) => in sustained batches the 57k overhead amortises to near-zero, confirming the warm operating point. BASELINE'S ACTUAL 100k COST (warm, measured rates haiku $0.0050, sonnet ~$0.0147): 2-call baseline = ~$1,975 (200k calls); haiku-only = ~$500 (100k calls); haiku+10%-sonnet band = ~$648 (110k calls). Worst-case (batching broken, every call cold): baseline ~$30k, haiku-only ~$7.6k. Harness reproduces these: docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hd_routing_cost_harness.py --dry-run prints the 100k projection {baseline 1970, haiku_only 500, banded_10pct 647}. QUALITY differential MEASURED in spike (findings L25-26): "Sonnet correctly flagged dead metaphors (e.g. pump for heart) that Haiku returned as top apt vehicles — calibration difference confirmed."
finding.variance: Cost: the cold-floor is n=1 (single probe, C6 flagged needs n>1), but the per-call WARM rate is anchored on n=400 real calls ($0.005, Phase2) plus two smaller runs (n=20, n=40), so the warm rate is well-bounded (~$0.005-0.014/call across three independent batches). The dominant cost variance is the warm-fraction (binary cold/cold-vs-warm per call), which the harness MEASURES directly by parsing cache_creation_input_tokens per call — currently NEEDS_ORCHESTRATOR_RUN to pin to the cohort. Quality differential (Sonnet catches dead metaphors Haiku misses) is observed but UNQUANTIFIED — no apt-rate delta has been measured between routes; the harness computes it with a Wilson 95% CI on n<=20 grades, which cannot bound a production rate (A3) — explicit refusal to extrapolate the quality delta past the cohort CI.
finding.quality_outcome: Against the LIVE/literary bar, routing is a COST lever, not a quality lever — and the cheapest route (Haiku-only) carries the SPECIFIC, MEASURED quality risk that defeats the product target: Sonnet uniquely flagged dead/conventional metaphors (heart->pump) that Haiku ranked as TOP APT (spike findings L25-26). Haiku-only therefore admits exactly the dead/synonym bridges the bar rejects. The Sonnet-as-prompt-engineer mitigation recovered Sonnet quality on FORMAT/aptness gates with "no measurable quality loss" (findings L242-246) at 65% cheaper, BUT that was never measured on the live-vs-dead discrimination axis specifically — so it is unproven for the bar that matters. The banded route is designed precisely to send the dead-metaphor-risk cases (high topic-vehicle cosine = same domain) to Sonnet while keeping the cheap path for the clear cross-domain bulk — preserving Sonnet's calibration where it is load-bearing. None of the three routes IMPROVES live-rate over the baseline; the best they do is match it more cheaply.
finding.cost_at_100k: Using the $0.07 cold floor amortised to the MEASURED warm rate (haiku $0.0050/call validated n=400; sonnet ~$0.0147/call content-derived + matched amortised-sys). At 100k topics: (a) current 2-call baseline = 200k calls, ~$1,975; (b) Haiku-only = 100k calls, ~$500; (c) Haiku-bulk + 10% Sonnet-escalation = 110k calls, ~$648 (5%=$574, 20%=$795, 30%=$942). One-time Opus calibration of a 200-pair set (batched ~20 calls) ~$1.50. Cold-batching worst-case ceiling: baseline ~$30k, haiku-only ~$7.6k. Assumptions: 700-tok prompts both models, 790-tok Sonnet / 700-tok Haiku outputs (measured from real chain data), Anthropic list prices, sustained batching keeps the 5-min prefix cache warm.
finding.scale_math: From the measured Phase2 anchor ($0.005/Haiku-call, n=400) the warm per-call rate scales linearly with call count: cost(100k) = N x (calls_per_topic x rate). Baseline = 100k x (1 x $0.005 + 1 x $0.0147) = $1,975. The 4x constraint: the "1x" reference is the existing per-topic enrichment substrate (80k synsets already enriched at ~$0.005-0.01/call, i.e. a few hundred $ historically); a 100k metaphor-link pass at ~$2k baseline / ~$0.5-0.65k routed sits comfortably inside ANY plausible 4x of that. CONCLUSION: <=4x is NOT a binding constraint and the baseline is ALREADY within budget at 100k — even the full 2-call baseline costs ~$2k, ~3x the haiku-only floor, not 30x. The whole spend axis spans $0.5k-$2k (warm), capped at $30k only if batching breaks. CI: warm-rate point estimate is tight (3 independent batches agree within 2x); I REFUSE to extrapolate the QUALITY delta between routes past the n<=20 cohort CI — that, not cost, is the open question.
finding.quality_risks: (1) Haiku-only admits dead/conventional metaphor (heart->pump) that Haiku self-rates apt and Sonnet rejects — directly measured, directly hits the LIVE bar. (2) The escalation band's same-domain-cosine signal inherits F4/F6: FastText cosine surfaces cross-domain candidates but cannot rank apt-above-inapt, and topic sense-snapping is noisy (anger->'make angry'), so the band will mis-route some cases. (3) The Sonnet-as-prompt-engineer few-shots are a FIXED, context-free template — if the gold examples don't cover a topic's domain, Haiku's live-rate degrades silently with no per-topic Sonnet check to catch it. (4) Routing optimises the WRONG axis: spend is already cheap (~$2k at 100k); shaving it to $0.5k saves $1.5k but risks the live-metaphor quality that is the entire product. (5) Optimising cost can MASK the real blocker — F1/F3 show candidate QUALITY/recall for abstract topics is the binding constraint, and no routing change touches that.
finding.harness_design: Delivered as runnable text at docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hd_routing_cost_harness.py (verified: `python3 hd_routing_cost_harness.py --dry-run` runs, makes ZERO API calls, prints the 100k projection). Two parts. PART 1 (cost): orchestrator runs each route on the 20-topic graded cohort; for every claude -p call, parse_cli_cost() extracts total_cost_usd + cache_creation_input_tokens (cold) vs cache_read_input_tokens (warm) from the CLI JSON, appended to hd_cost_log.jsonl; summarise_cost_log() then reports MEASURED $/call per model + observed warm-fraction + project_100k(). This turns the cold/warm assumption into an observation. PART 2 (quality): run R1 baseline (haiku+sonnet), R2 haiku-only (gold few-shots baked in, build via run_chain_spike.build_prompt with the proven template), R3 banded (needs_escalation(haiku_conf, topic_vehicle_cosine) decides Sonnet escalation) on the SAME cohort; grade every bridge with build_judge_prompt() (live/dead + linkage), calibrated first against the 11 human labels in judgements_provisional.jsonl (report judge-vs-human agreement before trusting it); compute apt(live)-rate per route with wilson_ci(). DECISION RULE: a cheaper route ships only if its live-rate Wilson lower-bound >= baseline live-rate point estimate AND judge-human agreement is acceptable. SQL anchor for the cosine band: SELECT cosine over synset_centroids for (topic_synset, vehicle_synset). Total harness spend ~ (40+20+~30) calls x ~$0.01-0.03 = ~$2-3, one-time.
finding.depends_on_separability: If the context-free apt-vs-inapt separability experiment SUCCEEDS: a cheap classifier can pre-filter candidates, so the LLM only adjudicates a high-precision shortlist — this AMPLIFIES H-D's value (fewer escalations needed, the band gets a real signal instead of noisy cosine), but H-D remains a second-order cost tweak on an already-cheap (~$2k) pipeline, so my verdict stays not_viable-as-primary / useful-as-trim. If it FAILS: cosine cannot separate apt from inapt, so the escalation band loses its principled signal and collapses toward "escalate on Haiku-confidence alone" — weaker, and Haiku-only's dead-metaphor leakage is then unmitigated except by per-topic Sonnet, which erases the saving. Either way the conclusion holds: routing does not move the live-quality frontier; it only rescales an already-affordable bill, and <=4x is not the binding constraint.
finding.one_line: The 2-call baseline already costs only ~$2k at 100k (warm-batch, measured) — well inside 4x — so <=4x is NOT binding; further routing (haiku-only ~$500, banded ~$650) trims a cheap bill but trades away the Sonnet calibration that uniquely catches dead metaphors, so routing is a cost-trim, not the answer to the quality problem.

finding.approach: H-E — caching & dedup amortisation. Vehicles/edges recur across topics; measure recurrence on existing dumps and estimate the amortisation factor a context-free edge cache buys at 100k.
finding.method: A context-free metaphor EDGE is (topic_synset -> vehicle_synset). The H-E thesis is that recurrence lets you compute a unit once and serve it to many topics, so the marginal edge cost falls. Two candidate cache units: (1) the vehicle NODE (river/fire/bridge recur as targets), and (2) the (vehicle V, property-cluster C) RELATION — compute V~C once, reuse for every topic that also has cluster C, per the brief's framing. The cache would be a keyed store: key on the reusable unit, value = the precomputed relation/feature-overlap, and assemble per-topic edges by joining the topic's clusters against the cache instead of re-generating. I measured recurrence at all three granularities (node / hop-edge / full topic->vehicle edge) on the 200 generated chains and the 200-topic phase2 apt+inapt dumps, then tested whether the (V,C) relation is actually a VALID cache key for an aptness decision (the precondition for any edge-producing reuse).
finding.measured_result: All reproducible via `python3 docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/measure_dedup_HE.py` (no API). RESULTS: (a) Chain recurrence (200 r1 chains, by synset_id): vehicle-NODE reuse 1.32x, intermediate-NODE reuse 1.58x, hop-EDGE reuse 1.06x, OVERALL candidate-edge dedup 1.05x. (b) Phase2 apt cohort (200 topics, 1112 pairs, 571 distinct vehicles): vehicle reuse 1.95x; 34.2% of vehicles recur across >1 topic; 66.2% of pair-slots have a cross-topic-recurring vehicle; top vehicles river=36 topics, fire=18, bridge=18, storm=17; (topic,vehicle) PAIR dup factor = 1.00 (no edge repeats). (c) Heaps' law fit distinct_vehicles ~ 1.93*slots^0.821 (beta<1, sublinear), vocabulary-clamped to 107,519 synsets => vehicle-NODE amortisation 2.0x@200 topics, 4.1x@10k, 9.3x@100k. (d) CACHE-VALIDITY (decisive): of 195 vehicles apt for >=2 topics, 33% (64) ALSO appear as INAPT for some topic; 66 direct (topic,vehicle) apt/inapt contradictions, driven by dead_metaphor / single_dimension verdicts (e.g. childhood->spring and spook->ghost are simultaneously feature-rich-apt AND inapt-because-conventionalised). (e) Exact cluster-profile collisions in lexicon_v2.db: 80,486 distinct profiles for 81,000 synsets => Haiku-propose cache hit ceiling 0.6%.
finding.variance: Bootstrap (n=500 topic orderings) on the phase2 vehicle amortisation factor: 1.947 with a degenerate 95% CI [1.947, 1.947] — the within-cohort factor is order-invariant (it is just total_slots/distinct over a fixed multiset). The REAL variance is cross-cohort: this is ONE cohort of 200 topics (the chain cohort is only 20 topics, n=11 human labels). The Heaps beta=0.821 is fit from a single 200-point rarefaction; I do not have a second cohort to bound its CI, so the 9.3x@100k node figure is an extrapolation with UNBOUNDED CI beyond the vocabulary clamp — I flag it as a hypothesis ceiling, not a measured value. The cache-validity numbers (33% flip, 66 contradictions, 0.6% profile-collision) are exact counts on existing data, not estimates, so they carry no sampling variance (they are lower bounds on a larger cohort if anything — more topics surface more flips).
finding.quality_outcome: H-E is a cost approach, not a quality approach — it does not change WHICH edges are produced, only whether they are recomputed. So its quality is exactly the quality of whatever it caches. The damning quality finding: caching at the (V,C) granularity SURFACES the dead-metaphor failure. The same vehicle+overlapping-feature is apt for one topic and a DEAD metaphor for another (childhood->spring inapt as 'thoroughly conventionalised, lost figurative force'; spook->ghost inapt as 'lexicalised'). Liveness is invisible to a feature-overlap cache key, so a context-free (V,C) cache would happily serve dead/conventional edges as if apt — directly violating the LIVE/cross-domain quality bar (status.md A1). Node-level caching (river, fire, bridge as recurring targets) is quality-neutral but also generation-free already (vehicles are synsets, SQL-derivable). Net: H-E adds zero new live metaphor and risks laundering dead ones if used as an aptness shortcut.
finding.cost_at_100k: Cold-call model: $0.07/cold call (G6, n=1, 57k-token system-prompt floor) + per-token. Baseline = 2 calls/topic (Haiku propose + Sonnet refine) => 200k calls @ 100k topics. H-E's amortisation does NOT reduce the call count, because both calls are topic-keyed (Haiku proposes vehicles FOR this topic; Sonnet refines THIS topic->vehicle chain) and the (topic,vehicle) edge dup factor is 1.00. The ONLY lever H-E touches is the $0.07 cold floor, and that is collapsed by BATCH cache-warming (keeping the 57k-token prefix warm in a 5-min window) — a property of the CLI already, available with or without vehicle dedup. System-prompt floor: $14,000 if every call cold (200k x $0.07); ~$70-$280 if batched at 200-50 calls/warm-window. So total ~= baseline token cost + ~$70-$280 amortised floor. H-E changes total 100k cost by 0 orders of magnitude vs the same baseline run batched without any dedup cache.
finding.scale_math: Cohort -> 100k. EDGE-level (the deliverable): each of 100k synsets is a topic exactly once => the (topic,vehicle) product has zero topic-side repetition => edge dedup = 1.00x BY CONSTRUCTION (confirmed: pair dup 1.00 in phase2, 1.05x overall on chains only because a handful of hop sub-phrases coincide). You cannot cache an edge for a topic you have not computed. NODE-level: vehicle reuse rises sublinearly (Heaps beta=0.821) toward a vocabulary ceiling: 2.0x@200, 4.1x@10k, 9.3x@100k topics — but nodes are FREE (synsets, already enriched, SQL-derivable), so this multiplier multiplies $0. (V,C)-RELATION level: the cache would hold ~823k (synset,cluster) cells, but the 33%-flip / 66-contradiction result proves a cached (V,C) relation does NOT determine topic->V aptness, so it cannot replace the per-(topic,vehicle) judgement. Haiku-propose caching keyed on cluster-profile: 0.6% hit ceiling (80,486 distinct profiles / 81,000 synsets). Conclusion: dedup is a CONSTANT-FACTOR win confined to the cheap/free recall layer and the already-available system-prompt batch cache; it does NOT change the 100k edge-cost order of magnitude. Confidence HIGH on the 1.00x edge structural argument (deductive + measured); MEDIUM on the 9.3x node ceiling (single-cohort Heaps extrapolation, clamped).
finding.quality_risks: (1) Dead-metaphor laundering: a feature-overlap (V,C) cache serves childhood->spring / spook->ghost as apt because they are feature-rich, but they are graded INAPT/dead — caching at this granularity systematically misclassifies conventionalised pairs as live. (2) Topic-conditioning loss: 33% of multi-topic vehicles flip apt<->inapt; any context-free cache that drops the topic context will emit the wrong verdict for ~1/3 of reused vehicles. (3) Sense-snapping noise (C13: anger->'make angry', heart->'playing card') propagates into every cached relation and is reused verbatim across all topics sharing the snapped cluster, amplifying a single snap error across many edges. (4) Cohort bias: the 9.3x node figure is one 200-topic cohort; abstract/literary topics (the product core) may have far thinner, more idiosyncratic vehicle sets, lowering real reuse.
finding.harness_design: Delivered as runnable text at `docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/measure_dedup_HE.py` (already executed by me, no API). It has four pure-data functions: chain_recurrence() [node vs hop-edge vs full-edge dedup on the 200 r1 chains, by synset_id], vehicle_amortisation() [cross-topic vehicle recurrence + Heaps' law fit on the phase2 apt cohort, vocabulary-clamped projection to 200/1k/10k/100k], cache_validity() [counts vehicles that flip apt<->inapt across topics + direct (topic,vehicle) apt/inapt contradictions — the (V,C) cache precondition test], profile_collisions() [exact cluster-profile collision ceiling for Haiku-propose caching, via sqlite on lexicon_v2.db]. It emits one JSON blob; reproduces every number in this finding. To extend: feed a SECOND independent topic cohort's apt-dump to bound the Heaps beta CI (the one gap I could not close), and (optional, would cost API the orchestrator tracks) re-judge the 66 contradictions with the LLM-judge to confirm the flip rate against fresh labels.
finding.depends_on_separability: If the apt-vs-inapt context-free separability experiment SUCCEEDS: it means a context-free function over the substrate CAN separate apt from inapt without per-topic LLM. In that world the per-edge judgement becomes cheap/SQL, and H-E's caching is even MORE redundant — you would just run the cheap separator over all candidates; there is nothing expensive left to amortise. H-E stays not_viable but for a happier reason (no expensive unit exists). If it FAILS: per-(topic,vehicle) LLM judgement remains the irreducible cost — and H-E still cannot amortise it, because the (V,C) cache I tested is proven invalid as an aptness decider (33% flip) and the edge product has no topic-side repetition (1.00x). So H-E is not_viable under BOTH outcomes; its verdict is independent of the separability result. The only thing that survives either way is the trivially-available system-prompt BATCH cache, which is not a dedup approach.
finding.one_line: Caching/dedup is a constant-factor win confined to the free recall/node layer and the already-available system-prompt batch cache — it does not change the 100k edge-cost order of magnitude (edge dedup is structurally 1.00x), and a feature-keyed (V,C) cache is an invalid aptness decider (33% of reused vehicles flip apt<->inapt) that would launder dead metaphors as live; not_viable as a standalone approach.

finding.approach: H-F — relational shortcuts: multiply context-free metaphor edges "for free" via SYMMETRY (topic->vehicle implies vehicle->topic) and TRANSITIVITY (a->b apt, b->c apt implies a->c apt), avoiding per-topic LLM generation for the multiplied edges.
finding.method: Take the set of LLM-generated/admitted apt topic->vehicle edges and close it under (1) reversal and (2) one-hop directed-graph transitivity, treating the closure as additional admitted edges at zero marginal API cost. Mechanism: a graph operation over already-paid-for direct edges, not new generation. The whole premise rests on two algebraic properties holding for metaphor aptness — which is exactly what I tested.
finding.measured_result: Ran docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hf_relational_shortcuts.py Part A (NO API) on metaphor_spike_apt/inapt_phase2_20260525*.jsonl + grading/sonnet_chains_provisional_r1.jsonl. Command: `python3 docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hf_relational_shortcuts.py`. RESULTS: (Symmetry) 0/1112 apt pairs have an apt reverse; 0/200 generated topic->vehicle endpoints have a generated reverse. (Stability) 66/1112 (5.9%) pairs are labelled BOTH apt AND inapt in the cohort — verified genuine context-dependence via the inapt explanations (e.g. advocacy->torch flagged dead_metaphor/cliché; appearance->mask single_dimension). (Transitivity) 11 bridge vehicles (topic AND vehicle) yield 228 derivable T->X->Y endpoints; only 15/228 (6.6%) carry any independent label; the 93.4% unlabelled are cross-domain garbage by inspection (ton->home, humbleness->nest, dietician->compass, recursion->eye); apparent precision 14/15 is CIRCULAR (the label exists only because T independently generated Y; it is NOT evidence the chain transmits aptness). (Multiplier) direct=1112, new transitive=214, nominal free multiplier ~2.4x (2x symmetry * 1.19x transitive). The CAUSAL symmetry test (does the JUDGE accept reverse edges) is NEEDS_ORCHESTRATOR_RUN: Part B of the same script prints a ready 20-pair reversal cohort + judge prompt; command `python3 .../hf_relational_shortcuts.py` already emits it, then wire each printed `{v} -> {t}` probe to lib/claude_client.py Haiku (~20 calls, <$1.50 batched).
finding.variance: Symmetry observational: reverse-apt 0/1112, Wilson 95% CI [0, 0.0034] — tight, but it only bounds the GENERATOR's reverse-production rate, not the JUDGE's reverse-acceptance rate (the generator was never asked to reverse), so it is suggestive not decisive. Transitivity labelled-precision 14/15, Wilson 95% CI [0.70, 0.99] — wide AND the metric is circular, so UNINFORMATIVE; the decision-relevant number is the 93.4% unverifiable/garbage fraction, which is a hard count not an estimate. Part B (n=20 reversal probe) is powered to settle the causal question: if true reversed-live-rate is ~0.2 vs forward ~0.65, expected 4/20 with Wilson CI [0.08, 0.42], cleanly separated from forward — n=20 is adequate.
finding.quality_outcome: FAILS the LIVE cross-domain bar, and worse, ACTIVELY INJECTS dead/garbage edges. (1) Symmetry is the textbook-asymmetric case: the cohort's own top-confidence apt pairs reverse into degraded metaphors — time->river (canonical live) reverses to river->time (forced); summit->success to success... I mean success->summit reverses to summit->success; wall->limitation, poison->disgust all degrade. This is exactly 'my surgeon is a butcher' != 'my butcher is a surgeon'. (2) Transitivity manufactures cross-domain nonsense (ton->home, humbleness->nest, dietician->compass, inbreeding->water) — 93.4% unverifiable, and 4 of 15 labelled transitive endpoints are independently INAPT. (3) The deepest evidence: 66 DIRECT pairs are simultaneously apt and inapt depending on sense/framing — if a single paid-for direct edge is this context-unstable, an edge synthesised by a graph rule that ignores context cannot possibly be reliable. Relational shortcuts surface dead/forced pairs, the precise failure mode the product must avoid.
finding.cost_at_100k: Marginal API cost of the multiplication itself = $0 (pure graph closure over already-generated direct edges). That is the entire and only appeal. But the brief's spend metric is the wrong frame here: the cost that matters is NEGATIVE quality cost. At 100k topics, naive symmetry+transitivity closure of the direct-edge set (~1.19x transitive growth measured, x2 symmetry = ~2.4x) would inject roughly 1.4x the direct edge count as DERIVED edges of which ~90%+ are dead/garbage/unverifiable — degrading the graph's live-metaphor precision and requiring downstream LLM-judge spend to clean up (which erases the 'free' saving and likely costs MORE than just generating fewer, real edges). Validation cost to even confirm a derived batch = full generate-then-judge per derived edge, i.e. no saving. Net: $0 to produce, but it does not reduce the real bottleneck (judged-live edges) and adds cleanup cost.
finding.scale_math: Cohort: 1112 direct apt edges over 200 topics (5.56 apt vehicles/topic). Linear extrapolation to 100k topics (assuming similar yield) ~ 556k direct apt edges. Symmetry closure adds up to 556k reversed edges (2x); transitive closure measured at +1.19x adds ~106k; nominal ceiling ~1.19M edges, a 2.4x multiplier. CONFIDENCE: I REFUSE to extrapolate this as a *useful* yield. The multiplier arithmetic is sound but the edges it produces fail quality: measured reverse-apt confirmation 0%, transitive verifiable-and-apt fraction <7% with the rest garbage, and 5.9% of even direct edges are self-contradictory. So the honest scale statement is: relational shortcuts scale the EDGE COUNT 2.4x for free but scale the LIVE-METAPHOR yield by approximately 0x (symmetry, pending Part B) to ~7% (transitivity). A 2.4x multiplier on a ~7%-precision derivation is not a path to high-quality 100k edges.
finding.quality_risks: (1) THE TRAP: the ~2.4x free multiplier lands exactly in the 'looks like it solves the 4x budget' zone — most seductive, most dangerous; an orchestrator under budget pressure could adopt it and silently poison the graph. (2) Asymmetry is intrinsic to metaphor, not a tunable — no threshold rescues reverse edges. (3) Transitivity compounds sense-snapping noise (F4) across hops: each hop's wrong-sense error multiplies. (4) Circular validation: the only 'confirming' labels for transitive edges exist because the endpoint was independently generated — they prove nothing about the chain. (5) Dual-labelling (66 pairs) means the underlying ground truth is itself context-dependent, so any context-free graph rule has an irreducible error floor. (6) Garbage edges in the graph degrade ALL downstream consumers (Forge ranking, graph nav), not just the new edges.
finding.harness_design: Written and verified at docs/inbox/2026-06-03-context-free-edges/artifacts/hf_relational_shortcuts.py. PART A (no API, already run): loads apt/inapt spike cohorts + chains; measures (A1) reverse-apt confirmation among the 1112 apt pairs and 200 endpoints, (A2) the apt-AND-inapt dual-label count, (A3) the 228 transitive T->X->Y endpoints via the 11 bridge vehicles with labelled-fraction + circular-precision, (A4) the nominal free multiplier + a garbage sample. Pure stdlib (json/glob/collections), reproducible, deterministic. PART B (orchestrator runs, ~$1.50): part_b_cohort() emits 20 distinct-synset high-confidence apt pairs and, for each, the reversed pair v->t plus a context-free judge prompt template ('Is "{v} is a {t}" a LIVE cross-domain metaphor or DEAD/INAPT? live|dead|inapt'). Orchestrator wires each printed probe to lib/claude_client.py Haiku, parses total_cost_usd into budget-ledger, computes reversed_live_rate; DECISION RULE: symmetry validated iff reversed_live_rate >= 0.7*forward_rate, else it is a quality trap (do not add reverse edges). No claude CLI is shelled by the script itself.
finding.depends_on_separability: Largely DECOUPLED, and that is the point. H-F is not a candidate-generation method over the substrate — it is a graph-algebra multiplier applied to whatever set of admitted direct edges already exists. So: (a) If the apt-vs-inapt context-free separability experiment SUCCEEDS, it gives a cheap context-free FILTER/scorer; that scorer would then REJECT the reverse/transitive garbage H-F produces (the filter is the very thing that exposes H-F's edges as inapt) — H-F still adds no net value, it just creates work for the filter. (b) If separability FAILS (the likely case, per C14/C16), there is no cheap context-free signal to clean up H-F's 90%+ garbage, so the only cleanup is full generate-then-judge per derived edge — which costs the same as generating real edges, eliminating the 'free' premise entirely. EITHER WAY H-F is not_viable; separability changes only HOW you would discover that its derived edges are bad, not WHETHER they are.
finding.one_line: Symmetry and transitivity are both invalid for metaphor — measured: 0/1112 apt pairs reverse to apt, transitive closure is 93%+ unverifiable cross-domain garbage, and even 5.9% of direct edges self-contradict — so relational shortcuts give a tempting ~2.4x free EDGE multiplier at ~0% live-metaphor yield; this is a documented NEGATIVE that protects the mission from a budget-pressured trap.
